name: Enhanced geothermal systems
applications: firm clean power anywhere with hot rock
reuse of oil and gas drilling skills
principle: Engineers create or enhance permeability in hot dry rock with hydraulic stimulation and horizontal drilling borrowed from oil and gas, so a circulating fluid can carry heat to a surface plant. NREL's 2024 baseline lists near-field EGS flash at 6,535 USD/kW and deep EGS binary at 13,508 USD/kW (dollar year not stated).

process_steps.name: Drill injector and producer wells into hot rock
Stimulate fractures to link the wells

source.note: NREL Annual Technology Baseline 2024, geothermal, read 25 October 2026

costs.metric: overnight capital cost, near-field EGS to deep EGS
costs.basis: NF-EGS flash 6,535 to deep EGS binary 13,508; dollar year not stated (base year 2022)

source.note: NREL Annual Technology Baseline 2024, geothermal, read 25 October 2026
IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Enhanced geothermal systems' 7 (2025); 'Closed-loop geothermal systems' 6 (2025)

advantages: Geothermal not limited to natural hydrothermal sites
limitations: Induced seismicity and water use need management
Costs fall only if drilling costs fall
